Getting Started

From zero to first signal

Install the CLI, create your workspace, define a monitor, and receive your first signal. Estimated time: 8–10 minutes.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Node.js v18 or later (for npm install), or Homebrew on macOS
  • An HTTPS endpoint you want to monitor (your own API, or use our example endpoint)
  • A SignalForge account — sign up free at app.signalforge.io
Free tier limits

Free accounts include 5 monitors, 30-second minimum interval, and 30-day signal history. No credit card required.

Step-by-step

01
Install the CLI
Install the @signalforge/cli package globally. You can use npm, yarn, pnpm, or Homebrew.
via npm bash 
$ npm install -g @signalforge/cli

+ @signalforge/cli@0.9.2
added 47 packages in 3.2s
via Homebrew (macOS) bash 
$ brew install signalforge/tap/signalforge

🍺 /usr/local/Cellar/signalforge/0.9.2: 52 files, 9.1MB

Verify the installation:

bash 
$ signalforge --version
signalforge/0.9.2 darwin-arm64 node-v20.10.0
02
Authenticate
Run signalforge auth login to open a browser-based OAuth flow. Your API key is stored in ~/.signalforge/credentials.
bash 
$ signalforge auth login

Opening browser for authentication…
✓ Authenticated as jamie@acme.io
✓ Workspace: acme-platform (ID: ws_01HX3K9F2J)
✓ Credentials stored: ~/.signalforge/credentials

If you prefer token-based auth (for CI environments), set the SIGNALFORGE_TOKEN environment variable instead. See API authentication docs.

03
Define your first monitor
Create a signalforge.yml file in your project root. This is a declarative definition of everything you want to monitor. Here's a real example for an API service:
signalforge.yml yaml 
# SignalForge workspace configuration
workspace:
  name: acme-platform
  environment: production

monitors:
  - id: payments-api-health
    name: "Payments API Health"
    type: http
    url: https://api.acme.io/v1/health
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 5s
    regions: [us-east-1, eu-west-1]
    expect:
      status: 200
      body_contains: "status": "ok"
      latency_p95_ms: 2000
    alert:
      - on: status_not_2xx
        severity: critical
        after_failures: 2
      - on: latency_p95_exceeded
        severity: warning
    tags:
      team: payments
      tier: tier-1

  - id: catalog-api-health
    name: "Catalog API Health"
    type: http
    url: https://catalog.acme.io/health
    interval: 60s
    timeout: 8s
    expect:
      status: 200
      latency_p95_ms: 3000
    alert:
      - on: status_not_2xx
        severity: warning
        after_failures: 3

# Alert rule: escalate if two tier-1 monitors are critical simultaneously
rules:
  - id: multi-service-outage
    name: "Multi-service outage"
    when:
      all_critical:
        - payments-api-health
        - catalog-api-health
    notify:
      - channel: pagerduty
        severity: critical
04
Sync to your workspace
Push your monitor definitions to SignalForge with signalforge monitor sync. This validates your config, diffs against current state, and applies changes.
bash 
$ signalforge monitor sync

Reading signalforge.yml…
Validating config… ✓
Diffing against workspace acme-platform…

  + payments-api-health   [CREATE]
  + catalog-api-health    [CREATE]
  + multi-service-outage  [CREATE]

Apply 3 changes? [y/N] y

✓ payments-api-health   created (mon_01HXK8A2BC)
✓ catalog-api-health    created (mon_01HXK8A2BD)
✓ multi-service-outage  created (rule_01HXK8A2BE)

2 monitors active. First check in ~30s.
05
Verify monitor status
After a few seconds, check that your monitors are running and healthy.
bash 
$ signalforge status

MONITOR                   STATUS    LAST CHECK      UPTIME
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
payments-api-health       ● OK      14s ago         100%
catalog-api-health        ● OK      22s ago         100%

2 monitors · 0 active signals · all OK
06
Configure notifications
Add a destination so you actually hear about problems. The simplest option is a Slack incoming webhook.
signalforge.yml — add destinations section yaml 
destinations:
  - id: slack-platform
    type: slack_webhook
    url: ${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}
    channel: #platform-alerts
    on_severity: [warning, critical]

  - id: pagerduty-oncall
    type: pagerduty
    integration_key: ${PAGERDUTY_KEY}
    on_severity: [critical]
Keep secrets out of YAML

Use environment variable references like ${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL} rather than hardcoding credentials. The CLI reads them from your shell environment at sync time.

07
Test your first alert
Use the CLI to fire a test signal to your configured destinations without triggering a real check failure.
bash 
$ signalforge test-alert --monitor payments-api-health --severity critical

Sending test signal…
✓ Delivered to slack-platform     (200 OK, 143ms)
✓ Delivered to pagerduty-oncall   (200 OK, 89ms)

Check your #platform-alerts Slack channel for the test alert.
You're done

Your monitors are running, alerts are wired up, and you'll hear about problems before your customers do. When an incident fires, follow the Incident Workflow runbook →

  • Add more monitor types — set up TCP, SSL, and DNS monitors for full-stack coverage.
  • Compose advanced alert rules — build multi-signal rules with AND/OR logic and maintenance window support.
